note: severity/category use the LLM contract vocabulary from SRS §5.2 (lowercase). overall_risk is what the server rule in FR-3.9 must derive, not the model claim.

findings.excerpt: Contractor shall provide revisions until Client is fully satisfied with the deliverables.
findings.why: Unlimited revisions with client as sole judge of satisfaction.

findings.excerpt: All work product, including preliminary concepts, sketches, and materials created by Contractor prior to the Effective Date, shall become the sole and exclusive property of Client upon creation.
findings.why: Assigns work created BEFORE the contract, and vests on creation rather than on payment.

findings.excerpt: Contractor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Client against any and all claims, damages, and expenses of any kind whatsoever arising from the Services, without limitation as to amount.
findings.why: Uncapped indemnity, explicitly without limitation as to amount.

findings.excerpt: For a period of twenty-four (24) months following termination, Contractor shall not provide design services to any business operating in the Client’s industry.
findings.why: 24-month industry-wide non-compete against a solo freelancer.

findings.excerpt: Client may terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reason or no reason, upon written notice, and shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress.
findings.why: Termination for convenience with no payment for work in progress.

findings.excerpt: Payment shall be due within ninety (90) days of Client’s acceptance of the final deliverables.
findings.why: Net-90, and the clock starts on acceptance rather than invoice.

findings.excerpt: Contractor shall bear all costs of software, fonts, stock imagery, and other materials required to perform the Services.
findings.why: All materials costs absorbed by contractor with no reimbursement.

findings.excerpt: Client shall pay all undisputed invoices within sixty (60) days of receipt.
findings.why: Net-60 financing of the client, and "undisputed" can stall a whole invoice.

findings.excerpt: Developer shall not disclose the existence of this engagement, the identity of Client, or the nature of the Services to any third party without Client’s prior written consent.
findings.why: Indefinite duration and bars naming the client — blocks portfolio use.

findings.excerpt: The hourly rate may be adjusted by Client upon sixty (60) days written notice to Developer.
findings.why: Client can unilaterally cut the rate on notice.

findings.excerpt: Developer shall address bug reports submitted by Client relating to the Services for a period of six (6) months following delivery at no additional charge.
findings.why: Six months of unpaid bug fixing with no defect definition.

also_acceptable.excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days written notice. Client shall pay for hours worked through the effective date of termination.
also_acceptable.why: Symmetric 30-day notice with payment for hours worked is fair; flagging it low is defensible, missing it is not an error.

documents.findings_note: ZERO findings expected. This fixture exists to catch a model that invents problems to look useful, and to exercise the empty-report UI state. Any high or medium finding here is a false positive and a test failure.
documents.missing_note: Deposit, late-payment interest, revision limit, kill fee, IP-on-payment, liability cap, scope-change process and portfolio rights are ALL present. An empty missing_clauses array is the correct output.

findings.excerpt: In the event Client requests reshooting of any footage for reasons other than technical defect, Producer shall reshoot at no additional charge.
findings.why: Unlimited free reshoots at client discretion — the expensive twin of unlimited revisions.

findings.excerpt: Producer shall pay Client a penalty of five percent (5%) of the total fee for each day of delay in delivery beyond the agreed date.
findings.why: 5% per day compounds to the entire fee in 20 days, with no cap and no carve-out for client-caused delay.

findings.excerpt: Producer may not display, reproduce, or reference the work in any portfolio, showreel, or promotional material.
findings.why: Absolute portfolio ban — for a video producer this is a career cost, not an admin detail.

fair_clauses_do_not_flag.excerpt: Client shall own all right, title, and interest in the final edited video upon full payment of all amounts due under this Agreement.
fair_clauses_do_not_flag.why: IP transfers only on full payment. This is the correct arrangement.

fair_clauses_do_not_flag.excerpt: The fee includes two (2) rounds of revisions. Additional rounds shall be billed at Producer’s standard hourly rate of $95 per hour.
fair_clauses_do_not_flag.why: Two rounds then hourly. This is the standard being recommended elsewhere.

fair_clauses_do_not_flag.excerpt: Fifty percent (50%) of the total fee is due upon execution of this Agreement, with the balance due within thirty (30) days of final delivery.

documents.fair_note: This fixture pairs genuinely bad clauses with genuinely good ones in the same document. Flagging anything in fair_clauses_do_not_flag is a false positive.

documents.note: Exercises FR-2.6. Word count is above the 4,000 Phase 1 cap, so no analysis should run and no LLM call should be made.

Rasterised pages, zero text layer. pdf-parse returns effectively nothing, so this trips the 200-word floor (FR-2.5). The user-facing message must mention a scanned image, since this is the most common real-world intake failure.
38 words. Paste-path equivalent of the scanned-PDF case.
Plain text renamed to .pdf. Magic bytes are 46 52 45 45, not 25 50 44 46. Exercises FR-2.3 — extension and client MIME type both lie.

fabricated_excerpts.excerpt: Contractor shall be paid a mandatory kill fee of forty percent (40%) upon termination for convenience.
fabricated_excerpts.why: Plausible, well-formed, and entirely absent. The clean case of a hallucinated protective clause.

fabricated_excerpts.excerpt: Writer shall provide unlimited revisions until Client is fully satisfied.
fabricated_excerpts.why: Lifted from fixture 01. Catches cross-document contamination.

fabricated_excerpts.excerpt: Client shall pay all undisputed invoices within sixty days of receipt.
fabricated_excerpts.why: PARAPHRASE of a real clause — drops "(60)" parentheses. Must be discarded. Documents the deliberate strictness of §5.3: near-misses are the hole a paraphrasing model slips through.
